title: The 10 Best Cordless Die Grinders
subtitle: Battery-powered straight and right-angle die grinders for grinding, porting and weld cleanup, ranked from live Amazon data.
intro: A cordless die grinder spins small bits and wheels fast for grinding, porting and deburring, without the air hose. We ranked 10 best-sellers from DEWALT, Milwaukee, Makita and value brands on rating, review volume and features (a brushless motor, speed control, batteries in the box and a brake).
data_source: Amazon product listings on the data_captured date. Prices, ratings and review counts change daily; check the listing before relying on a number.

avoid.name: 1100W Brushless Braking Die Grinder Compatible with Milwaukee Battery, 3 Level Variable Speed Up to 26000RPM
avoid.verdict: A Milwaukee-battery clone whose 1,100 W claim would need more current than an 18V pack is built to deliver.
reasons: 1,100 W at 18V is about 61 amps, far beyond what a compact power tool battery delivers continuously. Milwaukee rates its own M12 FUEL grinders at 0.3 to 0.4 HP (about 220 to 300 W).
It's rated 3.8 stars, the lowest of the die grinders we looked at except Milwaukee's slide-switch model.
Milwaukee's own M18 FUEL 2984-20 adds a real brake, five speeds and Milwaukee's warranty.

buyers_guide.q: What is a die grinder for?
buyers_guide.a: Grinding, porting, deburring, cleaning welds and cutting with small bits and wheels on a 1/4-inch shank. Think of it as a heavy-duty rotary tool.
Straight die grinders reach into holes and pipes. Right-angle grinders get into tight engine bays and corners where a straight body won't fit.
Air die grinders need a big compressor running constantly. Cordless models like Milwaukee's M12 FUEL are built to replace them for most shop work, without a hose.
A brake stops the bit quickly when you release the switch, so you can set the tool down sooner and it's less likely to grab.
Up to 25,000 RPM is typical. Lower speeds suit larger wheels and softer metals; variable speed lets you match the bit.
